rationale:
Issue dart-lang/tools#735 reports a bug where returning null from a JSON-RPC method causes an exception. The production fix changes `Object result;` to `Object? result;` in lib/src/server.dart, making the variable nullable to handle null return values. The trigger test 'Allows a `null` result' registers a method returning null and verifies the response includes `'result': null`, directly testing the reported defect. The minimized production patch contains only the single-line type annotation change with no refactoring, formatting, documentation, or unrelated logic. The trigger test is from the same fixing commit and semantically matches the issue description. Runtime evidence confirms: all checks passed, trigger reproduces only on buggy (buggy_differential=true, buggy_reproduces_only_triggers=true), fixed version passes (fixed_clean=true), deterministic across 3 repetitions. No duplicate root causes exist in active_same_project_root_causes.

All acceptance criteria are satisfied. (1) Issue dart-lang/tools#735 describes a bug where a null result causes an exception; the test 'Allows a `null` result' registers a method returning null and expects it to succeed; the production fix adds the nullable annotation `Object?` to the result variable. All three describe the same defect: missing null-safety annotation causing runtime failure when a method returns null. (2) The minimized production patch changes only `Object result;` to `Object? result;` on line 204 of lib/src/server.dart—a single-line type annotation fix with no refactoring, formatting, documentation, configuration, or test changes. (3) The trigger test is the upstream test added in the same commit; it directly tests the defect (method returning null) and does not depend on any new API introduced by the fix—the fix only corrects a type annotation, not an API surface. (4) active_same_project_root_causes is empty, confirming no duplicate within this project.
